title: The Fifth — Awareness Map event model (v0.1, definition only)
description: Events to preserve from day one so a future Farkındalık Haritası can show a user their own attention, resonance and repeated exploration across exploratory worlds. This is a DEFINITION, not an implementation: no collector, no analytics, no wiring exists yet. The map is a mirror of exploration behaviour, never a personality score, type, or diagnosis. Every field below is either already user-visible in the UI, or a content id, or a timestamp; nothing is inferred about the person.
principles: Attention, resonance and repetition are the only three quantities the map may ever derive: what was looked at, what the user said felt like them, and what they came back to.
No aggregate may be labelled as a trait ('you are X'). Aggregates are described as 'you kept returning to…', 'you marked… as familiar'.
Events record the user's own actions and explicit statements. The system never writes an inferred emotional state into an event.
Pseudonymous by default: user_ref is an opaque id issued by the app; nickname/avatar are not stored in events. No email, no device fingerprint.
User-deletable as a whole and per event; deletion cascades to any derived map.
Voluntary return only: lived_outcome events exist only if the user comes back and chooses to say something.
Schema is append-only across versions: fields may be added, never repurposed. schema_version travels with every event.

user_ref.description: Opaque pseudonymous id. Never an email or a device id.

session_ref.description: One exploration visit. Distinct from fifth_session_id (a Core conversation).

world_id.description: e.g. 'greek_olympus'. Worlds may differ in size and structure; the map must not assume 12.

world_version.description: Content version viewed, so later edits to content do not rewrite history.

world_entered.purpose: The user stepped into an exploratory world.

entry_point.description: Where they came from; 'after_anlat' means they arrived from an ANLAT Reveal.

figure_viewed.purpose: A figure came into focus (card opened, or in 3D: approached / selected). Not merely rendered on screen.

dwell_ms.description: Time in focus, capped at 10 minutes to avoid idle inflation. Attention, not interest.

order_in_session.description: 1 = first figure looked at in this visit.

figure_info_opened.purpose: The user opened the orientation / 'who is this' layer for a figure who they may know nothing about.

info_section.description: Which layer they read. Reading 'warnings' or 'sources' is worth knowing for content quality, not for the map.

story_door_viewed.purpose: A story door's text was shown in full to the user.

story_door_selected.purpose: The user chose a door (tapped 'bu bana tanıdık' / 'buradan gir' or equivalent).

doors_seen_before_select.description: How many doors of any figure were viewed in this session before this selection.

door_theme_attached.purpose: System-side: the content layer's tension_ref for the selected door is attached to the selection, so the map can later group by theme without re-reading content. Written by the app, not the user; carries no inference — it copies a content id.

resonance_marked.purpose: The user's explicit statement about a door or a Reveal. This is the only 'feeling' field in the model and it is the user's own words/choice, never inferred.

mark.description: 'feels_like_me' = user said so; 'continued' = proceeded without marking; 'skipped' = moved past; 'not_me' = explicitly declined.

free_text.description: Optional, user-typed. Stored verbatim, never summarised into a label.

core_conversation_started.purpose: The user opened a Fifth Core conversation from a door (KENDİNİ BUL → ANLAT hand-off).

fifth_session_id.description: Links to the fifth_sessions record. The map never reads the conversation text; it only knows a conversation happened and what came of it via reveal_saved.

entry_material.description: Whether the user added their own story before starting.

reveal_saved.purpose: The user chose to keep a Reveal. Saving is the user's act; unsaved Reveals leave no map trace beyond core_conversation_started.

door_id.description: Null if the conversation started from ANLAT without a door.

distinction.description: The portable one-line distinction, verbatim. The only Reveal content the map stores.

route_path.description: Which route the Core took; useful later for routing evaluation, not for the map's display.

lived_outcome_returned.purpose: The user came back voluntarily and said what happened. Never prompted by notification in v0.1; only available as a button on a saved Reveal.

outcome_mark.description: User-chosen. 'it_held' = the distinction still describes it; 'it_shifted' = something changed; no valence (better/worse) is recorded.

world_left.purpose: Session ended or user left the world; closes dwell accounting.

map_derivations_allowed.description: What the future Farkındalık Haritası may compute from these events, and the exact language it may use. Anything not listed is out of scope until reviewed.

attention.display_language: 'En çok burada durdun' — never 'seni en çok bu tanımlıyor'.

resonance.display_language: 'Bunu tanıdık buldun' / 'Bunu sakladın' — user's own acts, quoted back.

repetition.display_language: 'Buraya üç kez döndün' — a count, not a meaning.

forbidden: Any ranking of figures as 'your top gods'.
Any percentage or score per figure or tension.
Any sentence of the form 'sen … birisin'.
Any inference from skipped/not_me beyond 'you passed this'.
Cross-user comparison ('most people who chose this also…').

retention_and_control.default_retention: Until the user deletes; no silent expiry in v0.1 (decide before implementation).
retention_and_control.note: These controls are a precondition for collecting anything; the model is defined now so the first implementation does not have to guess which fields matter.

open_questions: Should dwell_ms be collected at all in the 3D client, where 'looking at' is ambiguous? Alternative: record only explicit focus/select.
Whether door_theme_attached should be a separate event or a denormalised field on story_door_selected. Kept separate so content can be re-tagged without rewriting user events.
How CLOSE routes appear on the map: a CLOSE is a completed visit with no distinction; it should count as attention, not as resonance.
